note: Kuma moved from the shared network monitoring to a new network of its own that Caddy is not on, so the status page returns 502 while the monitored sites work.

cause.title: refactor: own the status network in this stack
cause.author: Philipp Klinger
cause.patch:
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -99,7 +99,7 @@ jobs:
           networks="$(docker inspect --format '{{range $name, $_ := .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{$name}} {{end}}' "$(docker compose ps -q uptime-kuma)")"
           echo "Networks: ${networks}"
-          test "$(tr ' ' '\n' <<< "${networks}" | sed '/^$/d' | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "incident monitoring monitoring_outbound "
+          test "$(tr ' ' '\n' <<< "${networks}" | sed '/^$/d' | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "incident monitoring_outbound status "
 
       - name: No Docker socket mounted
diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
@@ -30,1 +30,1 @@ flowchart LR
-- The network `monitoring` belongs to [vps-edge](https://github.com/PhilippKlinger/vps-edge) and is internal. Caddy publishes only the status page, its API, badges and static files; everything else, including the dashboard and login, returns 404.
+- The network `status` belongs to this stack and is internal, so Kuma starts without vps-edge. Caddy publishes only the status page, its API, badges and static files; everything else, including the dashboard and login, returns 404.
diff --git a/compose.yaml b/compose.yaml
@@ -26,12 +26,13 @@ services:
     logging:
       driver: journald
-    networks: [monitoring, outbound, incident]
+    networks: [status, outbound, incident]
 
 networks:
-  monitoring:
-    # Created by vps-edge (internal, only Caddy and Kuma): the proxy never depends on this stack
-    name: monitoring
-    external: true
+  status:
+    # Owned here, so Kuma starts even if the edge stack is missing; internal: no route outside
+    name: status
+    internal: true
   outbound:
     # Route to the internet for the checks
     driver: bridge
